Metadata.description: English for work and study abroad: an honest diagnostic and preparation for IELTS, TOEFL and Cambridge exams with Murad Uzhakhov.

hero.title: English for work at international companies and study at top universities
hero.lead: For IT professionals job-hunting or already working at international companies, and students applying to top universities. An honest diagnostic using official materials, then work toward your actual exam, interview, or workplace communication.
hero.illustrationAlt: Line illustration of an open door with a certificate seal, revealing a university building and an office tower beyond it

about.title: About me
about.lead: I've long consumed information only in English — research, fiction, journalism. Combined with years living and working in the US and a C2 certificate, that gives me native-level command of the language.
about.educationValue: Translation and education degree, MA in Linguistics
about.mentorBody: I'll always offer moral support when it's needed. The exams are standard — the programme isn't: I choose materials and pace around how each student actually learns.
about.benefitBody: It's simple: every certificate you earn is my result too. That's how I see my real contribution to your life — and it's exactly why I teach.

approach.label: Approach
approach.title: Objective diagnosis
approach.body: I test using official materials, not guesswork. That shows where a student actually stands — and how far they can realistically move, based on their zone of proximal development.
approach.diagramAlt: Three concentric circles representing what a learner can do alone, the zone of proximal development, and what is not yet possible
approach.middle: Zone of proximal development — with a mentor's help
approach.quote: A student once came to me — told his level was A2. A couple of weeks of testing later: almost B2.
approach.cite: I show the real starting point — whatever it turns out to be.

method.label: Method
method.title: How I teach
method.lead: I teach through preparation for international exams. Why this way?

reasons.1: It gives us both a clear target, which shortens study time and makes it more effective.
reasons.2: It builds a healthy relationship between teacher and student: each of us owns our part of the result.
reasons.3: Your result is literally my result too — so my investment in it is guaranteed.
reasons.4: Exams test every language skill at once, so you learn to spot your weak points and work on them.
reasons.5: It gives an objective picture of how fast you're progressing — and a reason to adjust the programme in time.

method.footnote: After preparation, every student sits an international exam at an accredited centre and receives a certificate upon passing.

bridge.label: Method
bridge.title: Every student has their own breaking point
bridge.body: The exact place they used to get stuck. My job is to find it and build a bridge across it, with materials and pace built around you.
bridge.footnote: * Scores are a format example. Murad will fill in a real student's actual results.

materials.lead: Every book and test is standard, and you can check it yourself.

video.title: Video walkthrough

certificates.title: Level certificates
certificates.body: Real results from real students — B2, C1, C2 from accredited centers.

proof.chartAlt: Line chart showing an example of rising exam scores across four years
proof.chartCaption: Example visualisation. Real charts available per case, with each student's consent.
proof.tableCaption: * Format matches real student certificates. Numbers shown are illustrative.

items.1: You become genuinely more competitive — easier to get into a university abroad, relocate, or land a job.
items.2: You know for certain the time was well spent — the result is documented.
items.3: Learning further gets easier: each exam you pass builds confidence — in the language and in life generally.
items.4: Past B2–C1, you can stop studying the language on purpose and simply use it.
items.5: And yes — it's genuinely a good memory and a positive feeling.

guarantee.title: If I say you're ready, you'll pass
guarantee.body: My internal test decides whether you're ready to sit the exam. If I judge you ready and the result doesn't come — I cover your resit.

everyday.label: Beyond the exam
everyday.title: English changes where your information comes from

news.title: News
news.body: You read sources directly, instead of a delayed retelling filtered through translation.

health.title: Physical and mental health
health.body: Most current research and clinical guidance is published in English before any translation appears — sometimes without one at all.

culture.title: Science and culture
culture.body: Papers, books, podcasts — in the original, without distortion from retelling.

pricing.label: Pricing
pricing.note: per lesson · exact range confirmed at the first meeting

blog.lead: Notes on the books and articles Murad is currently reading, plus student case studies — no need to leave the page to see them.

case.title: Case study: A1 to C1 in four years
case.body: The full story behind one of the 54 — breaking point included.

science.title: Why science speaks English
science.body: English as lingua franca — and what it means for your career.

low.q: What if my level is very low?
low.a: That's fine — the diagnosis exists precisely to find your honest starting point, whatever it is.

it.q: Do you only work with IT professionals?
it.a: No, but IT careers and study abroad are where I have the most documented success stories.

group.a: No, one-on-one only — that way everyone owns their own result, which speeds up progress.

fail.q: What if I don't pass the exam?
fail.a: If I've sent you to sit the exam, I've judged you ready. If you don't pass — I cover the resit.

contact.title: Ready to find your breaking point?
contact.body: Message me on Telegram — I'll walk you through what's next and when we can run your first diagnostic.
contact.ps: P.S. The island of sanity is open for visits — no appointment needed.
